flags.name: --library-db
flags.summary: consult another index for calls THIS one cannot resolve (value receivers typed by name bind too; the manifest key libraryResolve opts a section in).

help: drag-lint index <path>                              [--db <file.sqlite>] [--watch [--interval N]] [--library-db <lib.sqlite> ...]
--library-db (v21, repeatable): consult another index for calls THIS one cannot resolve.
A hit is recorded by qualified NAME on refs.external_target -- never as a call_edges row,
because target_symbol_id is a NOT NULL FK into this db. A LOCAL answer always wins (the
cross-DB rung runs last), so adding a library can never change an edge that already existed.
Answers only when exactly ONE type and ONE member match; absence beats a guess.
A value receiver typed by NAME binds too (S.Read with S: TStream -> System.Classes.TStream.Read; refs.receiver_type_text
records the type). Without the flag, a manifest section opts in with "libraryResolve": true (default false):
index --all / index --project then open the platform library for the resolve pass only.
WALK SCOPING (any index run): [--exclude-under <dir>]... [--include-only <glob>]...
[--max-file-kb N] [--no-use-ignore] [--no-sql-ms] [--deep|--shallow]
--exclude-under and --include-only are repeatable and prune the walk;
--max-file-kb skips a file larger than N KB. --no-use-ignore opts OUT of the
.gitignore / .hgignore pattern files, which are honoured by default. A folder
holding a .scanignore MARKER file (contents never read) is always pruned with
its subtree; --no-use-ignore does not change that. --no-sql-ms indexes EVERY
.sql file, not just the MS*.sql migration scripts CREATE EXCEPTION text is read
from by default. --deep also records usage refs (--shallow is the default).
drag-lint index --project <file.dproj>              [--db <file.sqlite>] [--recompile|--rebuild] [--build-config <Release|Debug|name>] [--no-preprocess] [--dry-run] [--watch [--interval N]]
drag-lint index --scan-libraries-win                [--db <file.sqlite>] [--dry-run]   (Win32+Win64 Library+Browsing paths)
drag-lint index --scan-libraries-all                [--db <file.sqlite>] [--dry-run]   (every platform: +Android/iOS/Linux/OSX)
drag-lint index --all [--config <path>] [--only <Sec1,Sec2>] [--platform win32|win64] [--recompile|--rebuild] [--build-config <Release|Debug|name>] [--dry-run [--json]] [--jobs <n>]
SCAN TYPE is DECLARED BY THE TARGET, not by a flag. --project <.dproj|.dpr|.dpk>
(or a .dpr/.dproj manifest include) indexes the COMPILE CLOSURE: the project
members, the project-local units they transitively use, each one's sibling
.dfm, its {$I} includes, and the project file -- and NOTHING else. A loose
.pas nobody references, and anything on a Delphi Library/Browsing path, stay
OUT. A FOLDER target indexes the whole tree instead.
MODE is CHOSEN PER RUN. [--recompile] (DEFAULT) updates the index in place;
[--rebuild] first empties it of source, then walks. It deletes ROWS, not the
.sqlite: schema, migrations and settings survive and no open handle is
dropped. Implies --force-reparse. The two are mutually exclusive, and BOTH
apply to index --all: each manifest section honours the mode it was given.
[--force-reparse]: re-parse every walked file even when
path+mtime+sha are unchanged. Needed once per DB after an engine upgrade that
extracts something new -- see INBOX 2.3.
EVERY walk SWEEPS, and both halves delete symbols/refs/uses/docs with the
file: PRUNE drops indexed files that left the DISK; EVICTION drops files that
STILL EXIST and left the SCOPE -- a unit dropped from the .dproj, a copy under
an ignored folder, a tree a new [--exclude] now covers. Rows that outlive
their scope make every reference-derived answer (find-callers,
unused-public-symbol, doc facts) wrong. Bounded to the roots THIS run walked,
so indexing one project never purges another's rows from a shared DB, and
reported only when there is something to report. [--prune] forces the sweep
for a single-FILE walk, which does not sweep by default. [--no-prune] is the
one "delete nothing" switch, and it is a DRY LOOK: both sweeps are still
COMPUTED and REPORTED as "would remove" (count + a capped sample of paths),
nothing is deleted. Take it before a big run. Applies to index --all too.
A MALFORMED MANIFEST REFUSES the write (exit 2) -- beside the exe, a local
.drag-lint.json, or --config -- naming the file, the key path and both types
("indexes: expected object, got array"). Read verbs only warn.
A POSITIONAL .dpr/.dproj/.dpk beats the "project" key of the defaults file (one stderr note names the override); an explicit --project beats both.
--use-ignore is the default and is accepted so older scripts still parse; --dir <path> is the same as the positional <path>.
EXIT 1 when any file FAILED to store (an ERROR line on stderr names it and the file keeps its old rows) and, for index --all, when any section failed.

--name/--qname match CASE-INSENSITIVELY (Delphi identifiers are);

--kind literal|const|resourcestring|format|comment|doc|dfm-prop|sql-exception

searches STRING LITERALS ONLY -- string constants, resourcestrings,

entries.summary: Declare one exception class per distinct raise Exception.Create message, then rewrite the raise sites
entries.intro: Read this when a project raises bare Exception.Create with literal messages and you want one named exception class per distinct message. It is opt-in: add an "exceptions" block to drag-lint-lint.json (an empty one is enough; without it the verb says the feature is off and exits 0). It runs as a dry run, and --apply writes the classes into a managed block in your exceptions unit; the raise sites are then rewritten by `drag-lint lint <file> --fix --fix-rule raise-bare-exception [--apply]`.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint exceptions-sync [--profile <name>] [--db <file.sqlite>] [--config <lint.json>] [--apply] [--json] (materialise the project's derived exception classes)
help: drag-lint exceptions-sync    [--profile <name>] [--db <file.sqlite>] [--config <lint.json>] [--apply] [--json]   (materialise the project's derived exception classes)
Harvests every bare `raise Exception.Create('literal')` in the project and declares one class per
DISTINCT message inside a drag-lint:auto managed block in the exceptions unit. DRY RUN WITHOUT --apply.
Opt in with an "exceptions" block in drag-lint-lint.json -- an empty one is enough; key "unit" names
the unit (default uExceptionDefinitions, created if absent) and key "root" the ancestor (default Exception).
Each declaration carries its message in a same-line // comment, and THAT COMMENT IS THE KEY: rename a
generated class freely, but edit its comment and the next run adds a second class for the old message.
It is a VERB and not a --fix because its input is project-wide and its output is one file; the CALL-SITE
rewrite is the fix-it half and lives on `lint <file> --fix --fix-rule raise-bare-exception [--apply]`.

help: drag-lint lint-all           [--profile <name>] [--db <file.sqlite>] [--project <.dproj>] [--build-config <name>] [--rule <id>] [--disable id,...] [--output <report.txt>] [--json] [--labels] [--quiet] [--lint-third-party] [--no-preprocess]
--output <file>: the text report goes to the file; with --json or --format sarif the JSON / SARIF document does instead (a note on stderr, stdout stays empty).
--fix [--fix-naming] [--apply]: autofix every unit, as lint --fix (dry run without --apply)
--rule <id>: report ONLY that rule (one id per run; a comma list or a second, different --rule exits 2); naming an OFF-by-default rule opts it in
for the run (no --enable needed) -- the same contract as lint and lint-project.
--quiet: suppress per-file progress lines written to stderr
--project <.dproj|.dpr>: report ONLY on the units that project compiles
(its compile closure + their .dfm siblings). Use it when one folder holds
several projects, or when the DB spans more than the project you are reviewing.
taint-sql-injection / taint-command-injection / taint-path-traversal (store-backed): walk the index's data_flows
facts from a catalogued source to a sink; catalogues rules\taint-sources|sinks|propagators.json, extended by the
"taint" object of drag-lint-lint.json: sources sinks propagators sanitizers disable max_depth lib_depth max_rounds
follow_ambiguous weak_receiver_regex weak_severity_drop max_paths_per_sink second_order.
--fix [--apply]: AUTOFIX every fixable finding across the whole project.
DRY RUN WITHOUT --apply. This is what the Structure form's right-click
"Fix all in project" runs. It can rewrite many files at once -- dry-run first.

pitfalls: lint `<file>` is a strict SUBSET: project-wide rules can only fire in lint-all.

Without --apply it is a dry run (it prints the edits and writes nothing); with --apply it writes the comments, with a .bak unless --no-backup. Exit 0 on success including a dry run, 1 when some edits were refused because the index was stale (reindex, then re-run), 2 on a usage or database error.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint document-all [--profile <name>] [--stubs|--apply|--json|--no-backup|--include-accessors|--migrate-pure] [--db PATH] - document every public decl in every indexed unit (no project scope)
help: drag-lint document-all [--profile <name>] [--stubs|--apply|--json|--no-backup|--include-accessors|--migrate-pure] [--db PATH]               - document every public decl in every indexed unit (no project scope)

batch modes (--unit/--project/document-all) default facts-only: an empty tag is never written, <param> never gets a skeleton, and <summary> appears only when harvested from a nearby // comment; add --stubs to keep a fresh comment that has no facts block
batch modes also skip TRIVIAL Get*/Set* property accessors (impl body <= docs.accessor_trivial_max_lines, default 2) by default; add --include-accessors to document them too
drag-lint document --unit <file.pas> --strip [--apply|--no-backup] [--db PATH]   - REMOVE drag-lint-generated doc tags/blocks (marker-keyed; hand-written docs untouched)
--strip is also accepted on --qname/--project/document-all (strips just that symbol's doc region, or every file in scope); mutually exclusive with --stubs
<seealso cref> links to related symbols (callees + siblings) are emitted BY DEFAULT in every document mode;
--no-seealso turns them off. (--seealso is still accepted and does nothing -- it was the opt-in before it became the default.)
add --since [--base-dir <repoRoot>] to emit a git-derived <since> date; degrades silently when git is absent
@deprecated is auto-detected from the Pascal 'deprecated' directive on the decl -- no flag needed
--migrate-pure: regenerate a stored legacy <para>Pure</para> fact (purity v1). Without it a block whose ONLY difference is that line is left byte-identical, and doc-drift agrees
PROJECT TAGS: on a block reconciled across projects (dl:shared, or holding facts this index cannot see) the inbound entries -- Called from:, Used by:, Used in units:, Covered by: --
carry the projects that rendered them: Called from: [DataCopy,DataCopyTests]uX.Foo (uX.pas). A run adds/removes only ITS tag (the project's name, recorded in the index;
the DB base name for indexes built before 1.18.0); an entry goes when its set empties; untagged legacy entries keep the old rules

entries.title: convert-apply #migrate (member rename / DL_NONE)
entries.summary: #migrate Old -> New / Old -> DL_NONE inside a #convert block renames or deliberately breaks a member at every bound .pas access site
entries.intro: Read this when a component conversion changes the names of methods, events or properties the code uses. Inside a #convert block, #migrate Old -> New renames the member at every bound access site in the .pas; Old -> DL_NONE marks the site for hand conversion instead.

surfaces.usage: drag-lint convert-apply --unit <F.pas> [--unit <G.pas> ...] --rules <file> --db PATH [--db ...] [--only Name1,Name2,...] [--castlib <file>] [--apply] [--no-backup] [--no-warn-unlinked] [--no-reconcile-uses] [--no-reindex] [--format json|--json] (locates .dfm component instances matching a #convert rule and rewrites all 5 surfaces: declaration retype + uses-add + .dfm re-emit + property/event access-site rewrite + runtime-creator retype/TODO markers; without --apply this is DRY-RUN ONLY (preview, writes nothing); --apply writes for real with backups + a recovery.txt unless --no-backup; --format json emits schema apply/1 -- the six report surfaces plus a typed items[] carrying a machine-readable kind per line, so the conversion REMAINDER can be dispatched on instead of parsed out of prose, plus resolved_defaults[] (informational receipts, kept OUT of items[] because on a real form they run to thousands and would bury the remainder); --castlib names the .castlib whose enum blocks translate a #link value when the link carries a cast suffix; a source property some converted instance carries that no #link carries and no #ignore acknowledges is warned ONCE per (source type, property) as "dropped on N of M converted instance(s)" -- a minority count is the stronger signal -- and counted in json as unlinked_source_properties / unlinked_source_property_sites / unlinked[]; --no-warn-unlinked drops the warnings and keeps the count; the book's UNIT rules act on the unit too: #unuse Old removes it, #use New adds it to the implementation uses when absent from both clauses, #useswap Old -> New1[, New2] removes Old and adds each New once into the section Old was in (a unit that does not use Old gets no edit from the swap) -- a unit both added and removed is kept, an entry inside a {$IF...} region refuses the unit (exit 1, nothing written); with no sibling .dfm, no #convert block or no matching instance the unit rules run alone (component part skipped; a book with no unit rules still needs the .dfm, exit 1); json adds component_part, uses[] {action,unit,section,line,rule,reason}, uses_removed, uses_added; the To type's unit goes to the INTERFACE uses when the retyped field is declared in the interface, and is MOVED there from an implementation-only use (1.23.0);EVERY #convert block is validated and freshness-checked -- each #link/#default against its own From/To types, each #mapping against the blocks that #apply it -- with each path resolved segment by segment, no depth limit (a published leaf; PROGRESS (proptree, convert-scaffold): --progress-interval S (whole seconds; default 0 = OFF) writes one JSON line to STDERR at most every S seconds while the tree is built -- {"progress":{"elapsed_s":12.3,"verb":"proptree","class":"<qname>","depth":2,"max_depth":5,"classes_done":41,"classes_queued":7,"nodes":3114}} -- stdout is unchanged; S not decimal digits (x, -1, +3) or missing exits 2; every stderr line is flushed BEFORE the stdout document, which is written in one piece (a merged pipe reads notes, then the whole document); convert-apply / convert-validate reject --progress-interval as an unknown argument (exit 3) -- convert-apply takes --progress instead (1.33.0: one line per finished unit, see convert-apply); cancel = kill the process (the default write-back is kill-safe: each memoized type is its own SQLite statement)

entries.summary: Finds uses cycles among indexed units and, on request, proposes a followable refactoring plan to break them
entries.intro: Read this when the compiler complains about circular references or a project dependency graph feels tangled. a stand-down request (drag-lint shutdown --db <db>, or the IDE's Cancel) kills the build, rolls an --apply back and exits 1 ("cancelled -- rolled back"); --part all needs --apply, refuses --no-reindex; --library-db / --platform name the platform library --plan reads class ancestry from (default: the manifest's library for win64; --library-db none = no library); --rules-dir is forwarded to every --part all iteration; --stdio and --clientProcessId are accepted and IGNORED -- editor clients pass them;
stdio is the only transport, and --parent-pid is the shutdown watch that DOES act.

--proxy [--delphi-lsp <path>] [--trace <file>] [--merge-diagnostics] [--merge-completion] [--merge-hover] [--merge-definition] [--merge-budget-ms <n>] [--delphi-lsp-bits 32|64]: relay in front of RAD Studio's DelphiLSP,
so registering drag-lint as the Code Insight server keeps the compiler front end.
--trace appends every relayed LSP message to <file> with a direction tag (C>S / S>C); off by default.
--merge-diagnostics: append drag-lint's lint findings to DelphiLSP's publishDiagnostics (one notification, source-tagged); OFF by default.
--merge-completion: union drag-lint's completion items into DelphiLSP's reply, keyed on (label, kind); DelphiLSP's items first; OFF by default.
--merge-hover: append drag-lint's hover facts to DelphiLSP's hover after a --- rule, or answer with them alone when DelphiLSP has none; OFF by default.
--merge-definition: drag-lint's definition when DelphiLSP's is null or empty; answer references and workspace/symbol in the proxy (DelphiLSP has neither); OFF by default.
--merge-budget-ms <n>: per-frame budget for a merge handler; over budget forwards DelphiLSP's bytes untouched (default 300).
--delphi-lsp-bits 32|64: which DelphiLSP the proxy spawns (64 = bin64\DelphiLSP.exe, the default; 32 = bin\DelphiLSP.exe); --delphi-lsp <path> wins over it.
--full-rules: run the FULL rule set (built-ins included) out-of-process on every didSave and publish the complete finding set; OFF by default -- costs one `lint` run per save, reported on stderr.

lint-rules.title: local-var-casing
lint-rules.summary: Local variable name casing (naming, info, fixable)

lint-rules.title: locale-sensitive-conversion

lint-rules.title: loop-condition-invariant
lint-rules.summary: Loop condition never changes inside the body -- the loop cannot end or never runs again (bug-patterns, warning)

lint-rules.title: loop-control-flag
lint-rules.summary: Loop exit driven by a boolean flag -- consider Break (refactoring, hint)

lint-rules.title: loop-executes-at-most-once
lint-rules.summary: Loop body starts with Exit/Break/raise -- runs at most once (bug-patterns, warning)

lint-rules.title: loop-var-after-loop
lint-rules.summary: Loop variable used after the loop (data-flow, warning)

lint-rules.title: lossy-cast
lint-rules.summary: Ansi-narrowing cast of a Unicode string -- characters outside the code page are lost (W1057) (bug-patterns, info)

lint-rules.title: low-cohesion
lint-rules.summary: Class methods lack cohesion (LCOM4) (metrics, info)

lint-rules.title: magic-literal
lint-rules.summary: Unexplained numeric literal -- extract a named constant (refactoring, hint)

lint-rules.title: manual-inrange
lint-rules.summary: Two-sided inclusive bounds check on one value -- System.Math.InRange(X, A, B) states the intent and evaluates X once (refactoring, hint, fixable)

lint-rules.title: message-chain
lint-rules.summary: Message chain too long -- consider Hide Delegate (refactoring, hint)

lint-rules.title: method-could-be-static
lint-rules.summary: Method never uses Self or any instance member -- make it a class function or a free routine (refactoring, hint, fixable)

lint-rules.title: method-pascalcase
lint-rules.summary: Method/routine name casing (naming, info, fixable)

lint-rules.title: method-too-long
lint-rules.summary: Routine body is too long (complexity, info)

lint-rules.title: middle-man
lint-rules.summary: Class mostly delegates to one field -- Remove Middle Man (inline or expose the delegate) (refactoring, info)

lint-rules.title: misleading-indentation
lint-rules.summary: Statement is indented as if it were controlled by the preceding if/while/for but is not -- likely a missing begin/end (bug-patterns, warning, fixable)

lint-rules.title: mismatched-alloc-free
lint-rules.summary: Memory released by a call from a different family than the one that allocated it (GetMem/Dispose, New/FreeMem, ...) --... (resource-lifetime, warning, fixable)

lint-rules.title: missing-const-param
lint-rules.summary: Parameter is never modified, assigned or passed as var -- declare it const to avoid a copy or refcount (refactoring, hint, fixable)

lint-rules.title: missing-doc
lint-rules.summary: Public declaration has no DocInsight doc-comment (documentation, warning, fixable)

lint-rules.title: missing-inherited-ctor
lint-rules.summary: Constructor without an inherited call (bug-patterns, warning, fixable)

lint-rules.title: missing-inherited-dtor
lint-rules.summary: Destructor without an inherited call (bug-patterns, warning, fixable)

lint-rules.title: mixed-case-hex
lint-rules.summary: Hex literal mixes upper- and lower-case digits -- pick one case so the value reads consistently (structure, hint, fixable)

lint-rules.title: multiple-statements-per-line
lint-rules.summary: Two or more statements share one source line (structure, hint, fixable)

lint-rules.title: mutable-global-variable
lint-rules.summary: Mutable global variable -- shared mutable state (Fowler Global Data) (refactoring, info)

lint-rules.title: nativeint-truncation
lint-rules.summary: NativeInt/pointer-sized value cast to a 32-bit integer type -- truncates on Win64 (platform, warning)

lint-rules.title: needless-exit
lint-rules.summary: Exit as the last statement of a routine does nothing -- remove it (dead-code, hint, fixable)

lint-rules.title: nested-with
lint-rules.summary: Nested with statement (scope highly ambiguous) (structure, warning)

lint-rules.title: network-client-without-timeout
lint-rules.summary: Network client created without any timeout set -- a stalled peer blocks the caller indefinitely (security, warning)

lint-rules.title: nil-check-after-dereference
lint-rules.summary: Reference is dereferenced and only afterwards tested against nil -- either the use is too early or the check is redundant (bug-patterns, warning)

lint-rules.title: nil-comparison
lint-rules.summary: Prefer Assigned(X) over 'X = nil' / 'X <> nil' -- clearer, and correct for method-pointer references (bug-patterns, info, fixable)

lint-rules.title: nil-returning-call-dereferenced
lint-rules.summary: Member access on the result of a Find* routine that returns nil when nothing is found -- store the result and test it first (bug-patterns, warning)

lint-rules.title: nonminimal-bool
lint-rules.summary: Negated comparison can be written without not: use <> for not (A = B), = for not (A <> B), A not in S for not (A in S) (dead-code, info, fixable)

lint-rules.title: not-assigned-interface
lint-rules.summary: Interface variable dereferenced before assignment (nil interface call) (data-flow, warning)

lint-rules.title: not-comparison-precedence
lint-rules.summary: 'not A = B' parses as '(not A) = B' -- likely a bug; write 'not (A = B)' (bug-patterns, warning, fixable)

lint-rules.title: not-in-precedence
lint-rules.summary: 'not X in S' parses as '(not X) in S' -- almost certainly a bug; write 'not (X in S)' (bug-patterns, warning, fixable)

lint-rules.title: object-leak
lint-rules.summary: Created object may leak (not freed on every path) (data-flow, info)

lint-rules.title: off-by-one-count
lint-rules.summary: 'for I := 0 to X.Count/Length(X)' runs one past the end -- use 'to X.Count - 1' (or 'to High(X)') (bug-patterns, warning, fixable)

lint-rules.title: out-param-not-set
lint-rules.summary: out parameter not assigned on every path (data-flow, warning)

lint-rules.title: outputdebugstring
lint-rules.summary: OutputDebugString -- debug output left in code; remove it or guard with {$IFDEF DEBUG} (other, info, fixable)

lint-rules.title: overwrite-before-read
lint-rules.summary: Value overwritten before it is read (data-flow, warning, fixable)

lint-rules.title: param-name-prefix

lint-rules.title: parser-error
lint-rules.summary: Syntax error: parser failed to recognize this construct (bug-patterns, error)

lint-rules.title: path-traversal
lint-rules.summary: Concatenated path passed to a file API -- path traversal risk (security, warning)

lint-rules.title: pchar-arithmetic
lint-rules.summary: Pointer arithmetic on PChar -- unsafe and platform-specific (pointer size differs Win32/Win64). Use PChar[N] or string APIs (platform, warning)

lint-rules.title: platform-divergent-define
lint-rules.summary: A conditional symbol tested by IFDEF/IFNDEF/defined() is defined for one platform (Win32/Win64) of a config and not the other -- the... (project-wide, warning)

lint-rules.title: pos-for-contains
lint-rules.summary: Comparing Pos(...) with 0 or 1 is a substring test -- use Contains (Pos > 0 / <> 0 / = 0) or StartsStr/StartsWith (Pos = 1) (refactoring, hint, fixable)

lint-rules.title: pp-unresolved-if
lint-rules.summary: $IF names a constant the index cannot resolve -- the directive was taken as False, so the wrong branch (and include) may be indexed (bug-patterns, hint)

lint-rules.title: property-accessor-name
lint-rules.summary: Property accessor is not named F<Prop> / Get<Prop> / Set<Prop> -- the convention makes accessors findable (naming, info, fixable)

lint-rules.title: property-getter-with-effect

lint-rules.title: property-references-itself
lint-rules.summary: A property's read/write accessor is the property itself -- infinite recursion (bug-patterns, warning)

lint-rules.title: public-field
lint-rules.summary: Public field on a class breaks encapsulation -- expose it via a property (structure, info, fixable)

lint-rules.title: public-writable-field
lint-rules.summary: Public class field -- expose via a property instead (refactoring, info)

lint-rules.title: raise-bare-exception
lint-rules.summary: Raising the root Exception class -- raise a specific subclass so callers can handle it selectively (bug-patterns, warning, fixable)

lint-rules.title: raise-in-destructor
lint-rules.summary: raise inside a destructor -- an exception during cleanup aborts the rest of the teardown and leaks (bug-patterns, warning)

lint-rules.title: raise-in-finally
lint-rules.summary: raise inside a finally block masks the in-flight exception (bug-patterns, warning)

lint-rules.title: redundant-as-tobject

lint-rules.summary: 'if Assigned(X) then X.Free' -- the guard is redundant; Free and FreeAndNil already handle nil (resource-lifetime, info, fixable)

lint-rules.title: redundant-cast
lint-rules.summary: Cast of a value to the type it already has (no-op) (dead-code, hint, fixable)

lint-rules.title: redundant-continue-exit
lint-rules.summary: Continue or Exit as the last statement of a loop or routine does nothing -- remove it (dead-code, hint, fixable)

lint-rules.title: redundant-not-not

lint-rules.title: redundant-parentheses

lint-rules.title: referenced-never-set
lint-rules.summary: Private field is read but never assigned (dead-code, warning)

lint-rules.title: repeated-else-if-condition
lint-rules.summary: The same condition repeats in an if/else-if chain -- the later branch is unreachable (bug-patterns, warning)

lint-rules.title: repeated-type-switch
lint-rules.summary: Same case-selector repeated across 3+ methods -- Replace Conditional with Polymorphism (project-wide) (refactoring, info)

lint-rules.title: reraise-loses-stack
lint-rules.summary: 'raise E;' resets the stack trace -- use a bare 'raise;' to re-raise and preserve the original origin (bug-patterns, warning, fixable)

lint-rules.title: reserved-word-casing
lint-rules.summary: Reserved words must be lowercase (naming, info, fixable)

lint-rules.title: review-marker-malformed
lint-rules.summary: dl:ok names something that is not a rule id -- the marker suppresses nothing (review-markers, hint)

lint-rules.title: review-marker-placeholder-hash

lint-rules.title: review-marker-reason-unreviewed
lint-rules.summary: dl:ok reason has no REVIEWED <yyyy-mm-dd> stamp, or it is older than max_age_days -- re-read the reason and re-stamp it (review-markers, hint)

lint-rules.title: review-marker-stale
lint-rules.summary: dl:ok marker no longer matches the line it reviews -- the finding is reported again; re-review and re-mark (review-markers, hint)

lint-rules.title: review-marker-unused
lint-rules.summary: dl:ok marker records a finding that no longer occurs -- remove the marker (review-markers, hint, fixable)

lint-rules.title: self-assignment
lint-rules.summary: 'X := X' is a no-op self-assignment -- likely a copy-paste error (bug-patterns, warning, fixable)

lint-rules.title: separate-query-from-modifier

lint-rules.title: side-effect-in-short-circuit

lint-rules.title: sleep-in-vcl
lint-rules.summary: Sleep() on the main thread freezes the VCL UI. Use TTimer for delays or TThread.Sleep in a background thread (bug-patterns, warning)

lint-rules.title: split-variable
lint-rules.summary: Local reused for two unrelated purposes (disjoint lifetimes) -- Split Variable into two locals (refactoring, info)

lint-rules.title: sql-injection-concat

lint-rules.title: sql-update-delete-without-where
lint-rules.summary: UPDATE/DELETE literal without a WHERE clause changes every row -- add a WHERE, or mark an intended full-table statement with dl:ok (bug-patterns, warning)

lint-rules.title: stat-gated-destructive
lint-rules.summary: Destructive act gated on a file-existence check (a failed stat answers False) (bug-patterns, warning)

lint-rules.title: stream-read-result-ignored
lint-rules.summary: TStream.Read/Write result ignored -- a short transfer goes unnoticed; check the returned count or use ReadBuffer/WriteBuffer (bug-patterns, warning, fixable)

lint-rules.title: string-equality-comparison
lint-rules.summary: String compared with = -- consider SameText/SameStr semantics (bug-patterns, info)

lint-rules.title: suboptimal-math
lint-rules.summary: Power(X, 2), Power(X, 0.5) and Sqrt(Sqr(A)+Sqr(B)) have dedicated cheaper and more accurate functions: Sqr, Sqrt, Hypot (refactoring, hint, fixable)

lint-rules.title: swap-without-temp
lint-rules.summary: A := B; B := A does not swap -- A is already overwritten, so B is assigned to itself. Use a temporary (bug-patterns, warning, fixable)

lint-rules.title: syntax-error
lint-rules.summary: Source has a syntax error (bug-patterns, error)

lint-rules.title: taint-sql-injection

lint-rules.title: too-many-bool-fields
lint-rules.summary: Class has many Boolean fields -- they are probably a state machine or a set of flags in disguise (refactoring, info)

lint-rules.summary: Class has too many direct subclasses (NOC) (metrics, info)

lint-rules.title: too-many-parameters
lint-rules.summary: Routine has too many parameters (complexity, info)

lint-rules.title: try-except-swallowed
lint-rules.summary: try..except swallows the exception (no raise/log) (bug-patterns, warning)

lint-rules.title: type-name-prefix
lint-rules.summary: Type name must carry the configured prefix (naming, info, fixable)

lint-rules.title: ui-access-in-thread
lint-rules.summary: UI access inside a TThread.Execute (not thread-safe) (bug-patterns, warning)

lint-rules.title: ui-access-in-thread-transitive
lint-rules.summary: A TThread.Execute reaches, through resolved calls not marshalled by Synchronize/Queue, a routine that touches the UI -- the call path... (project-wide, warning)

lint-rules.title: unbalanced-begin-end
lint-rules.summary: Unbalanced begin/end (bug-patterns, warning)

lint-rules.title: unconditional-recursion
lint-rules.summary: Routine calls itself on every path -- it recurses until the stack overflows (bug-patterns, warning)

lint-rules.title: undocumented-check-suppression
lint-rules.summary: Range/overflow checking is switched off with no explaining comment just above -- say why it is safe (other, hint)

lint-rules.title: unit-name-matches-file
lint-rules.summary: Unit name must equal the file base name (naming, info)

lint-rules.summary: Unit is referenced but not listed in the .dpr (project-wide, warning)

lint-rules.summary: Third-party unit the project compiles via its search path is neither a project member nor in the library (project-wide, warning)

lint-rules.title: unit-too-large
lint-rules.summary: Unit exceeds N source lines (complexity, info)

lint-rules.title: unprotected-object-free
lint-rules.summary: Object created + freed without try-finally (resource-lifetime, warning, fixable)

lint-rules.title: unreadable-literal
lint-rules.summary: Long numeric literal without digit separators -- write 1_000_000 (Delphi 13) so the magnitude reads at a glance (modernize, hint, fixable)

lint-rules.title: unsafe-string-api
lint-rules.summary: Unsafe PChar string routine -- no length bound. Use System.AnsiStrings or TStringHelper equivalents (platform, warning)

lint-rules.title: unsafe-typecast-without-is
lint-rules.summary: Hard cast TFoo(x) of an object reference with no guarding 'x is TFoo' (bug-patterns, warning, fixable)

lint-rules.summary: Unsigned value compared with 0 or with its own type maximum (>= 0 / <= 255 on a Byte are always true, < 0 / > 255 always false) -- th... (bug-patterns, warning)

lint-rules.title: unused-local
lint-rules.summary: Local variable is never used (dead-code, hint, fixable)

lint-rules.title: unused-loop-variable
lint-rules.summary: for-loop counter is never used in the body -- the loop only repeats; check the intent (dead-code, hint)

lint-rules.title: unused-parameter
lint-rules.summary: Parameter is never used (dead-code, warning)

lint-rules.title: unused-private-member
lint-rules.summary: Private member is never referenced (project-wide, warning, fixable)

lint-rules.summary: Public symbol is never referenced (project-wide, info, fixable)

lint-rules.summary: Unit in uses is never referenced (project-wide, warning, fixable)

lint-rules.summary: Object used after X.Free (resource-lifetime, warning)

lint-rules.title: used-before-assignment
lint-rules.summary: Variable used before assignment (data-flow, error)

lint-rules.title: used-unit-not-resolvable
lint-rules.summary: Used unit resolves to no known unit (project/library/alias) (project-wide, warning)

lint-rules.title: useless-format
lint-rules.summary: Format('%s', [X]) just converts X to a string -- use X directly (or a string conversion) instead of formatting (dead-code, info, fixable)

lint-rules.title: uses-global-census
lint-rules.summary: How many of a used unit's globals and consts this unit actually draws, against how many that unit declares -- acknowledge a travels-toge... (project-wide, info)

lint-rules.title: uses-movable-to-implementation
lint-rules.summary: Interface uses entry is needed only by the implementation section -- move it to cut coupling and compile time (project-wide, hint, fixable)

lint-rules.title: virtual-method-in-constructor
lint-rules.summary: Virtual/dynamic method called from a constructor (bug-patterns, warning)

lint-rules.title: virtual-never-overridden
lint-rules.summary: Virtual method with no override anywhere in the project -- the virtual dispatch buys nothing (project-wide, hint, fixable)

lint-rules.title: wait-while-holding-lock
lint-rules.summary: Blocking call (Synchronize, WaitFor, Sleep, SendMessage, dialog) while a lock is held -- risk of deadlock (bug-patterns, warning)

lint-rules.title: weak-hash-for-secret

lint-rules.summary: A security-named variable is generated with System.Random (not a CSPRNG) (security, warning)

lint-rules.title: win64-pointer-cast
lint-rules.summary: Pointer cast to a 32-bit integer type -- unsafe on Win64 (platform, warning, fixable)

lint-rules.title: with-hides-outer-symbol
lint-rules.summary: A bare name inside a with body binds to the with-target while an outer scope declares the same name -- the compiler never warns (bug-patterns, warning)

lint-rules.title: with-multiple-items
lint-rules.summary: 'with A, B do' lists multiple objects -- name resolution is highly ambiguous; use explicit qualified access (structure, warning)

lint-rules.title: with-statement
lint-rules.summary: 'with' statement makes symbol scope ambiguous (structure, info)

lint-rules.title: write-only-local
lint-rules.summary: Local assigned but never read (data-flow, info, fixable)

lint-rules.title: writeln-in-source
lint-rules.summary: Direct WriteLn call -- consider a logger (other, info)
